name: Civic Nationalism
summary: Civic nationalism defines the nation as a community of citizens held together by shared political institutions, liberal principles and the continuing consent of its members, not by ethnic descent. Membership is open to anyone who accepts the constitution, and the nation is the unit of democratic self-rule. It says little on economic policy, where adherents range from left to right.
scope: The mainstream liberal or democratic strand: Renan's 1882 lecture, Kohn's civic/ethnic distinction, Habermas and Sternberger's constitutional patriotism, and liberal nationalists such as Miller, Tamir and Kymlicka, with parties like the SNP and Plaid Cymru as modern examples. It excludes authoritarian state nationalism and ethnic or cultural nationalism. Many economic and social answers are low-confidence because the ideology is a theory of membership, not a full program.

keyFigures.name: Ernest Renan
keyFigures.role: Author of What Is a Nation? (1882), often seen as an early civic nationalist.

keyFigures.name: Hans Kohn
keyFigures.role: Among the first to distinguish civic from ethnic nationalism (1944).

universal-healthcare.rationale: Civic nationalism says nothing on health policy directly; the liberal-nationalist claim that shared national identity sustains welfare solidarity points mildly toward public provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Civic nationalists span left and right on economic policy (SNP to US Republicans of the Civil War era), so there is no common line.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The ideology defines membership, not economic order, and its adherents split on markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Adherents include social-democratic and market-liberal nationalists; the ideology is silent on ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No shared position; the liberal-nationalist case for national solidarity is used by both redistributive and non-redistributive parties.

unions-good.rationale: Labour policy is outside the ideology's core and adherents differ.

property-fundamental.rationale: Civic nationalism's rights language is political and civic rather than specific to property, and adherents differ.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The ideology is silent on corporate regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Liberal nationalists argue shared identity underpins welfare-state solidarity, so a typical adherent resists dismantling it, though this is inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: No source ties civic nationalism to any view on enterprise ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-rights and constitutional commitments of civic nationalism; adherents are divided on security trade-offs.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is outside the ideology and adherents are split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Civic nationalists oppose racism but differ on legal speech limits, as liberal traditions themselves do.

strong-leader.rationale: Constitutional and democratic procedure is central, so bypassing gridlock through a strong leader runs against it; authoritarian state nationalism is a minority variant.

state-harmful.rationale: Civic nationalism makes the state and shared citizenship the basis of the nation, so it cannot regard the state as unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: The ideology has no position on firearms; US and European adherents differ.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; adherents divide.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Outside the ideology's scope and adherents are split.

decide-locally.rationale: Civic nationalism centres the national citizenry as the unit of self-rule, though devolved arrangements are accepted; inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy is outside the ideology.

traditional-family.rationale: Civic nationalism is deliberately neutral on private culture and family form, and adherents differ.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Equal citizenship regardless of group suggests support, but the ideology does not address it and adherents vary.

abortion-legal.rationale: A moral issue outside the ideology; adherents split.

more-religion-public.rationale: Membership is by citizenship and political principle rather than religion, and Renan says the nation is not defined by religion, so a larger public religious role is not part of the project.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Civic nationalists oppose racism, but whether to adopt active remedies is contested among them.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Even civic nationalists keep a shared national identity and heritage; Renan stresses a rich legacy of memories, and critics note civic models still depend on culture, though the ideology does not make culture the criterion of membership.

gradual-change.rationale: Adherents range from reformers to revolutionary founders (1776, 1789), so no common stance.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Membership is open to anyone who accepts the civic principles, so restriction is not required, but the ideology sets no immigration level and many adherents back controls.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Civic nationalists value national self-rule, while constitutional patriotism extends to the EU, so adherents split.

free-trade.rationale: Trade policy is not part of the ideology.

nation-first.rationale: The nation is the unit of self-determination, but liberal nationalists hold that identity-based loyalty is morally bounded, so a typical adherent rejects pure national egoism without endorsing global cooperation unconditionally.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between universalist and sovereignty-first views.

open-borders.rationale: Civic nations are open to joining by citizenship but still presuppose a bounded self-governing people; eventual open borders is not their goal.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental economics is outside the ideology.

revolution-justified.rationale: Civic nationalism emerged from the American and French revolutions, but modern adherents favour constitutional change; adherents differ.

experts-over-public.rationale: Popular sovereignty and consent of the governed are central, so rule by experts over the public runs against it.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred from liberal-democratic orientation; the ideology is silent on economic planning.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred from liberal-democratic framework; no source addresses it, and it is an extreme position alien to civic nationalists.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Civic nationalism organises politics around individual citizens rather than state-recognised functional bodies; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Civic nationalism is tied to constitutional democracy and plural public debate, and authoritarian forms are described as a deviant state-nationalist variant.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Civic nationalists include republicans (France, US) and monarchist states (UK, Scotland's SNP accepts the Crown); divided.

democracy-best.rationale: Civic nationalism grounds the nation in the consent of its citizens, and Ipperciel argues it historically shaped modern democratic government.

direct-votes.rationale: Popular sovereignty is central, but representative versus direct forms are not settled by the ideology.

workers-councils.rationale: Citizenship in a general national electorate, not class bodies, is the basis of political membership; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: Renan holds that the inhabitants of a territory have the right to be consulted, and civic nationalist parties (SNP, ERC) pursue independence by consent, though SEP notes self-determination does not always mean a separate state.

natural-rulers.rationale: Equal citizenship and consent of the governed leave no room for innate fitness to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Adherents range from pacifist constitutionalists to heirs of revolutions; no common line.

war-builds-character.rationale: Renan values shared sacrifice as binding the nation, but civic nationalism does not glorify war; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Civic membership is defined by citizenship and political principle rather than religion, and Renan denies religion defines a nation, though the strictness of separation varies (France versus UK).

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Civic nationalism grounds law in a constitution and citizens' consent, not scripture or religious identity.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The ideology treats the state as the instrument of the self-governing nation; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The defining claim of civic nationalism is that the nation is built on citizenship and shared political values, not ethnicity or descent; Renan says man is not a slave to his race.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Renan locates national unity in will and shared memory, and civic nationalism offers no class-conflict theory of history; inferred.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Equal citizenship and rights are central; equal outcomes are not, and the ideology is silent on distribution.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; civic nationalists differ on how to reconcile a single civic nation with indigenous claims.

civilizational-union.rationale: The nation is the civic community of citizens, not a civilizational bloc; inferred, though constitutional patriotism has supranational applications on political rather than religious grounds.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rights are built into the civic constitutional framework, though civic republican strands stress duties; adherents differ in emphasis.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Citizen consent and public deliberation are central, so handing decisions to algorithms does not fit; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Civic nationalism defines the nation by present consent, Renan's daily plebiscite, rather than a lost order.

direct-action.rationale: Change is expected through constitutional politics and public reasoning; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly alien to a modern constitutional-state ideology; inferred.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not addressed; alien to the ideology.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Not addressed; Marxian exploitation theory is no part of civic nationalism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class dictatorship contradicts equal citizenship and constitutional consent.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal-democratic framework.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: No such theory appears in civic nationalism; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Civic nationalism treats the state as a legitimate common institution of citizens; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; liberal and communitarian strands differ.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Liberal nationalists defend a national group interest in sustaining culture alongside individual rights, though civic nationalism emphasises individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Rawlsian liberal nationalists may accept national service, but adherents differ.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Participation and citizenship are central; the ideology is not exit-centred.

state-as-business.rationale: Citizens are members of a political community, not customers; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; the welfare-solidarity argument suggests some sympathy, but adherents split.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not part of the ideology; the claim is typical of populist right movements.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Civic nationalism's 20th-century revival is credited with opposing racism, and it rejects race as a basis of membership.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation runs through citizens in a common electorate and public sphere; inferred.

total-state.rationale: Constitutional limits, rights and a pluralist public sphere are core to civic nationalism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Civic nationalism rests on consent and constitutions rather than myths of decadence and rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Renan rejects annexing territory against the wishes of its inhabitants.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on a constitution and consent, not personal oaths.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Enlightenment-liberal orientation of civic nationalism.

universal-morality.rationale: Constitutional patriotism rests on universal principles of rights, though the ideology does not take a developed metaethical stance.

single-common-good.rationale: Habermasian legitimacy rests on fair procedures among differing views rather than one substantively shared good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Civic nationalists may support Israel as a national self-determination case or criticise its ethnic character; no common line.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Civic nationalism defines membership by citizenship, not descent, so a descent-based right of return conflicts with it.

revive-national-language.rationale: Civic nationalism is not tied to a single language, though some civic movements (Plaid Cymru) support language revival; adherents differ.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule of law and constitutional procedure are central; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Renan makes the nation's consent to live together the foundation of political legitimacy, and civic nationalism treats self-determination of citizens as central.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; adherents include religious believers.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Liberal nationalists tie welfare to national solidarity, but civic membership is open to immigrants who become citizens; adherents split on the eligibility of non-citizens.

class-collaboration.rationale: Renan and later civic nationalists stress shared national solidarity, but they do not prescribe labour relations.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Renan makes a rich inherited legacy of memories part of what a nation is, so sacrificing heritage institutions cuts against it.

workers-nation.rationale: Civic nationalism's national community cuts across class, so it does not call for class organisation along national lines; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Equal citizenship regardless of group is a core principle.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal-secular orientation.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Civic nationalism rejects racial membership criteria and its revival is credited with opposing racism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Not part of civic nationalism, which treats the state as the common institution of citizens; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Habermas argues immigrants need only accept the constitution's principles, not the host culture, though some civic nationalists (France) expect cultural integration.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy of replacing a native population presupposes an ethnic conception of the nation that civic nationalism rejects.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral design is not part of the ideology.

national-mission.rationale: American and French civic nationalism often carry universal-mission themes, but the ideology itself does not, and adherents differ.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic restriction conflicts with equal rights of citizens.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Rule-of-law constitutionalism implies accountability for state abuses, but the ideology does not address it directly.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range across economic views.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Ethnic descent is not the basis of civic nationhood, and the ideology is credited with opposing racism.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Civic nationalism extends membership and equal rights to all citizens regardless of ethnicity or culture.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed; civic nationalists in settler states differ.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal citizenship under common law is a civic principle, though some civic states allow group exemptions.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religion is not a criterion of membership and restrictions conflict with liberal rights.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religious-cultural measure outside the civic framework; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: French civic nationalism favours it, other civic states do not.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine alien to civic nationalism; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Renan's nation is a continuing act of consent, a daily plebiscite, and civic nationalism treats membership as voluntary.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilism is not part of civic nationalism; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Civic membership is open by citizenship regardless of group, and Renan says the inhabitants of a territory have the right to be consulted.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed; adherents accept state coercion in various forms.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social-Darwinist national competition is characteristic of ethnic nationalism, not civic; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Sternberger's constitutional patriotism was framed as defending the democratic order against internal threats, though adherents differ on bans.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Civic republican thought is close, but the ideology does not adopt it explicitly.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional government with a pluralistic liberal-democratic constitution is the object of civic loyalty.

vanguard-party.rationale: Contradicts consent and plural democratic citizenship.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Civic nationalism holds that a shared civic identity can unite culturally diverse citizens, though critics (Yack and others) doubt abstract principles generate solidarity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Election by citizens is the standard civic-democratic mechanism; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Constitutional rights are the object of civic loyalty, so adherents resist suspending them, though state-nationalist variants differ.

party-controls-media.rationale: Public-sphere deliberation is central to constitutional patriotism, so state or party control of media conflicts with it.

party-commands-army.rationale: The armed forces belong to the constitutional state in civic nationalism, not to a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Civic nationalism makes citizenship the open door to membership, which favours accessible naturalisation, though it sets no specific term.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred from liberal-democratic orientation; party organisation is outside the ideology.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Constitutional patriotism has been applied to the EU, but civic nationalists such as the SNP and Plaid Cymru are split on pooling; contested.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; depends on the constitution.

clerical-rule.rationale: Political authority rests on citizens' consent, not religious office.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Renan's nation is bound by shared sacrifice, and civic nationalism does not endorse revolutionary defeatism; inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Liberal rights and a public sphere of open reasoning argue against censorship; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal-democratic orientation.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed; civic republican strands differ from liberal ones.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Renan holds that the inhabitants should be consulted on territory, so civic nationalists support reunification only by consent; split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Civic nationalism is neutral on culture in principle, but adherents differ on whether to rank cultures.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from secular, civic membership criteria; not directly addressed.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Civic nationalism makes membership a matter of citizenship open to anyone, opposing descent as the criterion of belonging.

minority-language-support.rationale: The SEP says liberal nationalist identities can be open to minorities, but language policy is contested within civic nationalism (France versus Scotland, Catalonia).

religious-exemptions.rationale: Equal citizenship favours uniform law, while pluralism favours accommodation; adherents differ.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; Mill is a liberal source, but the ideology is not about it.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Civic nationalism seeks political self-rule via constitutional means and does not require a transformed property system; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Popular sovereignty implies a constitution made by citizens, as in civic nationalism's origins in 1776 and 1789, but the ideology does not require a specific procedure.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberal rights are the object of civic loyalty; authoritarian state nationalism is a minority variant.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: SEP notes the debate between cosmopolitan duties and special duties to compatriots; liberal nationalists are split.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; depends on the national constitution.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Renan makes the inhabitants' wishes decisive over territory rather than historic claims.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Constitutional limits on power fit civic constitutionalism, though the ideology does not address term limits.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Civic nationalism is a theory of membership and has no environmental doctrine; no position follows from its principles.

collective-defense.rationale: Liberal nationalists accept mutual obligations among states of shared liberal values; inferred, since the sources do not discuss alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Renan holds that a nation's inhabitants have the right to be consulted on their territory, so a transfer without consent has no legitimacy.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Liberal constitutional patriotism favours church-state separation, not state control of churches' property; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Constitutional patriotism makes shared institutions the focus of loyalty, which a non-partisan figurehead symbolises; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Because the nation rests on continuing consent, forcibly holding an unwilling region contradicts it, though some adherents defend territorial integrity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Liberal nationalists such as the SNP and Plaid Cymru favour national autonomy within larger unions; inferred for a region keeping its own system.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Renan rejects dynastic right and divine legitimacy as the basis of a nation, which rests on citizens' consent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Adherents span left and right on economics, so there is no common line on tax design.

character-from-environment.rationale: Renan denies that race or descent makes the nation and stresses shared experience and choice; inferred as a mild lean to nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Constitutional patriotism rests on loyalty to a constitution that binds all officeholders.

space-expansion.rationale: Civic nationalism says nothing on space policy.

mixed-constitution.rationale: It requires a democratic constitution but is silent on blending aristocratic elements; adherents would not insist on either.

leader-cult.rationale: The ideology is defined against authoritarian state nationalism, and a leader cult contradicts citizens' consent and equal membership.

equal-parenting.rationale: Nothing in the theory of membership bears on custody law.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Civic nationalism stresses a shared citizenship over class division; inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Civic nationalists range from left to right on economics, so there is no settled position.

refugee-return.rationale: Liberal civic nationalism is rights-based and favours return for displaced citizens; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Civic nationalism defines the nation by citizenship and consent, not descent, so nationality alone gives no claim to foreign territory.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Liberal principles and constitutional loyalty rule out punishing a change of religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory dress codes conflict with the liberal principles civic nationalism rests on; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Constitutional patriots such as Habermas favour European integration while nationalist parties differ, so adherents split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Civic nationalism rejects ancestry as the basis of political community, so descent-based unions have no pull.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Liberal nationalists such as Kymlicka support minority self-government within a state; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Civic membership is open to all who accept the constitution, so minorities pursue equal rights where they live; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Civic nationalism sees political institutions and ideas as central to the community; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is outside the civic nationalist program; no settled position.

no-bailouts.rationale: Economic stance varies across civic nationalists; no settled position.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Constitutional patriotism makes loyalty to the constitution and liberal principles central, so courts may constrain majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Adherents range from left to right and there is no settled position on quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Civic nationalism is open and liberal and does not call for a closed bloc; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: No settled position; adherents split with their wider economic views.

moral-incentives.rationale: Civic nationalism says little on work incentives; inferred from its liberal and market-tolerant range.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Civic nationalism rests on democratic consent, so a small armed vanguard sits badly with it; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Membership as equal citizens under a constitution tells against inherited rank; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Civic nationalists value shared national memory in Renan, but also a plural, critical view of history, so adherents split.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Civic nationalism rests on consent and self-determination, which rule out one society governing another.

patriotic-education.rationale: Constitutional patriots want loyalty to shared political institutions taught, while avoiding ethnic pride.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Civic nationalism says nothing on this, and its adherents span left and right.

public-money-creation.rationale: Civic nationalism is a theory of membership with no monetary stance.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Civic nationalism has no economic theory, and adherents span left and right.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Renan and consent-based self-determination give past rule no special claim; inferred from these principles.

delink-world-market.rationale: Liberal civic nationalists generally accept open economies, though some favour protection; inferred, weak lean.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This is a Marxist thesis outside civic nationalism, which has no position.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Civic nationalism stresses equal citizenship under liberal institutions, which points against private discrimination; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional patriotism makes loyalty to an entrenched liberal-democratic constitution and its rights the basis of the nation.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from Renan's view that the inhabitants' consent should settle territory, which treaties imposed without consulting a people lack.

elective-rulers.rationale: A nation of citizens under a constitution implies leaders chosen by that political community, as in constitutional patriotism.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from Renan's collective will and democratic majority rule, though liberal nationalists also protect minority rights.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Constitutional patriotism makes loyalty run to the constitution, so a ruler who breaks it forfeits that loyalty.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Civic nationalism puts sovereignty in the citizens' democratic institutions, normally an elected parliament.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; civic nationalism is a theory of membership, not of animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; civic nationalism has no stated position on the use of animals.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from liberal nationalists such as Miller, who ground welfare in national solidarity and mutual duty among citizens.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Civic nationalism and constitutional patriotism rest on active participation of citizens in shared political institutions.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed; civic nationalism does not theorise mass culture.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed; civic nationalism does not theorise how power is kept.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from left to right on economics.

native-born-offices.rationale: Civic nationalism defines membership by citizenship, so naturalised and native-born citizens hold equal rights, including to office.

party-own-road.rationale: The statement concerns communist parties, which this tradition does not address.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range across the economic spectrum and the tradition is a theory of membership.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Civic nationalism rests on consent of the inhabitants, so it rejects irredentist claims based on past wars and ancestry.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Civic nationalism rejects descent-based membership; political leadership by ancestry contradicts equal citizenship.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional patriotism grounds national loyalty in liberal democratic principles, which anti-fascism expresses.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from liberal democratic commitments that reject both fascism and communism as totalitarian; adherents differ on equivalence.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from the liberal democratic tradition, whose mainstream scholarship holds slavery was the central cause.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the civic emphasis on an inclusive national identity, which shapes how a nation treats symbols honouring figures like slaveholders.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; civic nationalism is a theory of membership, not of gender.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed; civic nationalism has no stated position on domestic violence.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the universalist liberal principles of constitutional patriotism, which hold democratic constitutions are broadly applicable.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Constitutional patriotism and liberal democracy hold the army subordinate to civilian constitutional authority.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from left to right on social policy.

filial-duty.rationale: Civic nationalism is a theory of membership and says nothing on family duties; liberal nationalists treat it as a matter for personal and cultural choice.

office-by-exam.rationale: Membership rests on consent and citizenship, so offices are naturally filled through the citizens' institutions rather than by examination alone; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Liberal nationalists accept some protection of national assets, but the economic question divides adherents across left and right; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Constitutional patriotism rests on liberal individual rights, which fits easy divorce; the sources do not address it, so inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Constitutional-democratic nationalism assumes representatives who exercise judgment within a constitution, not mandated delegates; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Adherents range from left to right on economic policy, so there is no common line on pension design.

land-use-tenure.rationale: A liberal constitutional order protects individual property rights, so community-held land is not a civic-nationalist aim; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: A liberal-democratic constitution of the kind civic nationalists defend rests on parliamentary control of the public purse.

single-official-language.rationale: Renan says language does not define the nation, while some liberal nationalists want a common public language and others protect minority languages; adherents split.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Liberal nationalists accept duties to compatriots and some limits on outsiders, but open membership makes a blanket ban unlikely; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Civic nationalists oppose discrimination but are divided over judging it by outcomes instead of intent; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The ideology is a theory of membership and has no stated view on consumer culture.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The doctrine does not address covert support for foreign insurgents; liberal nationalists emphasise self-determination but adherents would differ.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Renan holds the nation rests on the consent of its inhabitants, and liberal nationalism defends self-determination, so forcible intervention to keep an ally in line is rejected.

corporate-influence.rationale: Civic nationalists stress equal citizenship and democratic self-rule, which undercut undue corporate influence, but they give no settled economic line.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Self-rule favours protecting democratic processes, but liberal civic nationalists value open civil society and adherents split.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Civic nationalism is a theory of membership and has no position on birth-rate policy; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Civic nationalists span left and right and have no common line on local property restrictions.

job-guarantee.rationale: Civic nationalists range from left to right on economic policy, with no shared view on job guarantees.

democratic-peace.rationale: Civic nationalists are liberal democrats who generally accept that democracies seldom fight each other; inferred from liberal nationalism.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Constitutional patriotism rests on loyalty to the constitution and its law, and nations exist by members' consent, so a general rejection of the duty to obey is unlikely; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Self-determination implies respect for other nations' self-rule, but liberal nationalists accept intervention against atrocities.

industrial-unions.rationale: Civic nationalism has no position on union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Civic nationalism defines membership by shared citizenship and constitutional principles, so conspiracy theories about a minority contradict its premise.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Civic nationalism has no position on marriage law.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Constitutional patriotism rests on open democratic institutions and accountable government, which points toward access to information; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Civic nationalism is silent on where goods are produced.

informal-organisation.rationale: Civic nationalism rests on shared political institutions and citizens' formal membership, so permanent institutions rather than informal groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Constitutional patriotism makes the constitution central, but Habermas also favours international legal cooperation, so adherents split.

religious-nation.rationale: Renan says race, language and religion are not what makes a nation, and civic nationalism defines membership by citizenship.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Civic nationalism sees nations as communities of equal citizens with the right to self-rule, so tribute and ritual submission do not fit; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Civic nationalists span left and right and take no common line on regional revenue sharing.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Civic nationalism is liberal in outlook and does not seek common ownership of productive property; inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: Civic nationalism says nothing on communism; adherents vary.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: No common line; civic nationalists range from left to right on public service delivery.

religion-illusion.rationale: Constitutional patriotism rests on a secular constitution and does not claim religion is an illusion; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Liberal-leaning civic nationalists generally accept capitalism as a source of prosperity; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Liberal nationalism works through law and equal citizenship, not economic transformation; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Welfare solidarity is stressed in liberal nationalism but no view on childcare provision is documented.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Because membership rests on citizenship and not on culture, language purism has no place in the civic idea; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Consent and constitutional commitment imply binding agreements with internal nations, though the sources do not discuss treaties.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Civic nationalism centres on the nation-state and its constitution, not communes; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Membership rests on citizenship and consent, so steering the majority into minority regions to bind them runs against the principle of equal political membership.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Civic nationalism has no stated view on a third way between capitalism and communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Renan holds that the present inhabitants must be consulted on territory, so ancestry does not trump current residents.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Civic nationalism rests on liberal-democratic values, which reject denial; inferred from that basis.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Constitutional patriotism rests on liberal rights and equal citizenship, which exclude criminalizing same-sex relations.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Loyalty is to a liberal-democratic constitution and the continuing consent of members, which requires free opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Civic nationalism's liberal principles protect freedom of conscience and speech; religion is no basis of membership.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Consent of the governed and self-determination are the core of the theory, which rules out exploitative rule of overseas peoples.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A question of Islamic law that the theory of membership does not address.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Renan says religion is insufficient to define the nation and the state rests on a constitution and consent, not religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Renan's daily plebiscite and constitutional patriotism emphasize active citizen consent, though direct workplace participation is not addressed.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Adherents range from left to right, so there is no common view.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Equal citizenship and liberal rights suggest recognition, but the sources do not address it; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Outside a theory of membership; adherents split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The ideology spans left and right and takes no stance on the division itself.

alienated-labor.rationale: Adherents include liberals and conservatives who mostly do not accept this Marxian critique; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Membership is open to anyone who accepts the constitution, and religion cannot define the nation.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority rests on citizens' consent and the constitution.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents split between strict civic secularism, as in France, and liberal tolerance of religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal equal-citizenship principles.

social-market-economy.rationale: Liberal nationalists defend welfare solidarity among citizens, but adherents range from left to right on economics.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Civic nationalism makes the nation the unit of self-rule, which implies the right to defend it; inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Liberal nationalists stress solidarity and fair shares among compatriots; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; civic nationalists are split, with the sources noting constitutional patriotism's link to the EU.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Civic nationalism rests the nation on citizens' continuing consent and shared institutions, which is incompatible with hereditary office.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: A theory of membership, it says nothing on credit, and adherents range from left to right on economics.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Civic nationalism says little on economics, and adherents split on international lenders' conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: Membership is open to all who share the political community, and consent of all members is the basis, so wealth tests contradict it.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Civic nationalism has no stated position on women and nature, and adherents are indifferent.

reification.rationale: Civic nationalism offers no theory of market society, so this is outside its scope.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Civic nationalism says little on media ownership, and adherents range across the economic spectrum.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Constitutional patriotism makes loyalty to a liberal-democratic constitution and its rule of law the core of national identity.

racial-franchise.rationale: Renan, the key source, rejected race as a basis of the nation, and civic nationalism defines membership by citizenship, not descent.

online-participation.rationale: Civic nationalism has no stated position on online participation, though its emphasis on public deliberation does not rule it out.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the constitutional-patriotism emphasis on open democratic deliberation and accountable institutions.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Renan held that religion does not make a nation, and citizenship-based membership rules out religious tests in marriage law.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Citizenship-based membership treats all citizens equally regardless of religion, and Renan rejected religion as a criterion of belonging.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not stated in the sources; inferred from the liberal-democratic emphasis on active citizenship and Habermas-style deliberative democracy that civic nationalists draw on.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Not stated in the sources; inferred from the liberal, secular-constitutional strand, which expects religious doctrine to adapt to a shared civic order.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Civic nationalism rests on citizens as equal members of a shared political community, so great wealth able to dominate politics undermines it; inferred, as adherents range across economic views.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Civic nationalism grounds membership in shared political principles rather than identity, so equal treatment of citizens in service follows; inferred from the liberal principles in the sources.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Civic nationalism is a liberal, inclusive form of membership based on constitutional principles, which is incompatible with state promotion of unbelief.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not addressed directly; the civic strand's liberal-democratic stress on rights and rule of law favours reformed policing over abolition. Inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Civic nationalism treats all citizens as one demos, which cuts against communal quotas, but liberal nationalists accept power-sharing in multinational states; adherents are split.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Civic nationalism is not an economic program, and adherents range from left to right on welfare.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' views on term limits follow their wider politics.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology concerns who belongs to the nation, not how votes are cast.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents have no common position.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the civic strand's liberal principle of equal membership and equal treatment of citizens.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the liberal principle of equal citizenship that civic nationalism relies on.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the civic idea that belonging rests on participation in shared institutions rather than descent, which favours including long-term residents locally.

rent-control.rationale: Civic nationalism is a theory of membership and says nothing on housing; adherents range from left to right.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the liberal strand's general acceptance of established property and legal rights; the ideology does not address intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from its liberal, consent-based view of the nation, which sits badly with drilled youth movements run for national ends.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The ideology does not address defence basing, and adherents in parties such as the SNP and mainstream liberal nationalists differ.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Civic nationalism asserts national self-rule but does not address foreign bases, and adherents differ on alliances.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from liberal-democratic commitments to human rights and public acknowledgement of historical wrongs; not a stated tenet.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The ideology is silent on economic policy and its adherents range from left to right.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-democratic state's accepted use of lethal force to protect citizens; pacifism is not part of the doctrine.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Renan states that nations are not eternal, that they began and will end, and that national unity is built by forgetting and historical error rather than by ancient descent.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Civic nationalism has no position on the theory of sex and gender, so this is split or indifferent.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Feminist theory is outside the ideology, so no position can be derived.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Renan values the shared memory of sacrifice, but a liberal civic nation honours its dead in a secular, restrained way rather than as martyrs and saints; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Renan calls the nation a spiritual principle, but civic nationalism treats politics as consent, institutions and constitutional debate rather than a cosmic struggle; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Civic nationalism ties the nation to citizens of a state, not to diasporas, and does not address this question.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from its stress on shared political institutions and constitutional principles over shared culture as the basis of the nation.

god-not-male.rationale: Religious language is outside the ideology, so no position can be derived.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Religious authority is outside the ideology, so no position can be derived.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Membership is open to anyone who accepts the constitution regardless of descent, so reserving economic life for a national majority contradicts its core inclusiveness.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from its view that the nation is a body of citizens, not a people by descent, so borders need not follow where a people live.

missingStatements.text: Membership of the nation should depend on shared citizenship and loyalty to the constitution, not on shared ancestry or culture.
missingStatements.rationale: This is the defining claim of civic nationalism, and constitutional patriotism proposes attachment to the constitution rather than culture.

missingStatements.text: A nation exists only so long as its members continue to choose to live together.
missingStatements.rationale: Renan describes the nation as a daily plebiscite resting on the consent and desire to continue living together.

missingStatements.text: Immigrants should be expected to accept a country's constitutional principles but not to adopt its culture.
missingStatements.rationale: Habermas holds that immigrants to a liberal-democratic state need only accept its constitution's principles.

missingStatements.text: Disputes over which state a territory belongs to should be settled by the consent of its inhabitants.
missingStatements.rationale: Renan says the inhabitants are the ones with the right to be consulted on territory.

notes: Civic and ethnic nationalism are rarely pure: critics (Yack, Tamir, Brubaker) argue civic nations still rely on culture, and French assimilationist and Habermasian pluralist strands answer immigration and culture questions differently.
